summary: A Stack Overflow question from January 2019 in which AnnaMP, a beginner, reports that cv2.imshow() on macOS Mojave with Python 3.6 and OpenCV 4.0.1 opens an empty window even though cv2.imread loads the butterfly.jpg image correctly. Attempts such as absolute paths, startWindowThread, and namedWindow did not help. Commenters asked for build information and suggested a related OpenCV GitHub issue. The asker later answered that the cause was an installation conflict: Python 3.6 and 3.7 coexisted, and OpenCV was built against 3.7, so running brew link python to the 3.7 installation fixed it.
one_line: Beginner's Stack Overflow question about an empty imshow window on macOS, resolved as a Python 3.6 versus 3.7 OpenCV installation conflict.
key_facts: The question was asked on 2019-01-23 by user AnnaMP on the OpenCV answers forum (Stack Overflow-style site).
The asker's code used cv2.imread('butterfly.jpg', 0) followed by cv2.imshow('Butterfly', img) and cv2.waitKey(0).
The imshow window opened with the correct measurements for the image but displayed no image content.
The asker confirmed the image was loaded correctly because print(img) showed the correct array and cv2.imwrite saved a black-and-white copy.
The asker used Python 3.6 on macOS (Mojave) with cv2 version 4.0.1.
Attempts that failed included using an absolute path, adding cv2.startWindowThread() and cv2.namedWindow('Butterfly'), and adding cv2.namedWindow('Butterfly', cv2.WINDOW_NORMAL).
The build information showed an interpreter at /usr/local/opt/python/bin/python3 with version 3.7.2, while the asker believed they were using Python 3.6.
The asker had installed OpenCV with 'brew install opencv', which placed it under python3.7 site-packages, and had manually symlinked a cv2 .so file.
Commenter LBerger identified the root cause of the mismatch between Python versions as the source of the problem.
A linked GitHub issue (opencv #8885) was considered but judged different because those users saw only the window title bar.
The accepted answer, posted 2019-01-29 by AnnaMP, says the problem was an installation problem fixed by uninstalling Python 3.6 and running brew link python to the 3.7 installation.
The question was viewed 13,560 times and had 1 follower at the time of capture.
